D: Pongo and Perdita set out across England to rescue their puppies from Cruella De Vil.
P: Serve the snacks when the puppies settle in front of the TV for their favourite dog show.
S: Pongo and Perdita's spotty cheese straws
Puff pastry with cheddar, parmesan, black olives and nigella seeds

Flaky puff pastry twisted with sharp cheddar and parmesan, spotted with black olive and nigella seeds, baked crisp and golden. Lay out 2 thawed puff pastry sheets and brush with beaten egg. Scatter one with 80g grated cheddar, 30g parmesan, 50g finely chopped black olives and 1 tsp nigella seeds. Lay the second sheet on top and press down firmly. Cut into 1.5cm strips, twist each a few times and lay on lined trays. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden and crisp.
Barn honey shortbread with warm milk dip
Buttery honey shortbread, with warm milk for dipping

Buttery honey shortbread fingers baked pale gold, with little cups of warm vanilla and honey milk for dipping, just like the barn stop. Beat 200g soft butter with 70g caster sugar and 2 tbsp honey until pale, then mix in 300g plain flour and a pinch of salt. Press into a lined 20 x 30cm tin, prick all over and bake at 160C for 25 minutes until pale gold. Cut into fingers while warm and cool in the tin. Warm 600ml milk with 1 tbsp honey and 1 tsp vanilla and serve in small cups for dunking.
Sooty puppy black sesame potato chips
the puppies rolling in soot to disguise themselves

Thin crisp potato chips tossed in a sooty seasoning of black sesame, smoked salt and crumbled nori, the puppies' chimney-soot disguise. Slice 4 large potatoes paper thin on a mandoline, soak in cold water 20 minutes, then dry thoroughly. Fry in small batches at 170C for 3 minutes until crisp and golden, and drain. Grind 2 tbsp toasted black sesame seeds, 1 sheet of nori and 1 tsp smoked salt to a coarse dust. Toss the hot chips in the seasoning and serve in a big bowl.
M: Lamb mince with carrots and peas under buttery mash
Lamb mince simmered with onion, carrot, peas and stock, topped with buttery mash and baked at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.
Nanny's roast beef and Yorkshire puds
Nanny looking after the house and the puppies

Mustard-crusted beef topside roasted pink, with puffed Yorkshire puddings, crunchy roast potatoes and lashings of onion gravy. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with 1 tbsp English mustard and salt and roast at 200C for 50 minutes for medium, with 1kg parboiled potato chunks in oil around it. Rest 20 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk. Heat 1 tsp oil in each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin at 230C, pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes. Fry 1 sliced onion, add 1 tbsp flour and 400ml beef stock and simmer.
W: Soft buttermilk cookies iced half white, half chocolate
Soft vanilla cookies baked at 180C for 12 minutes, iced half in vanilla glaze and half in chocolate glaze.
K: Vanilla and chocolate shakes poured side by side, whipped cream and chocolate drops

Half chocolate, half vanilla thickshake poured side by side so it swirls into spots, with whipped cream and chocolate drops on top. Blend 4 scoops vanilla ice cream with 300ml cold milk and 1 tsp vanilla, and pour into a jug. Blend 4 scoops chocolate ice cream with 300ml cold milk and 1 tbsp cocoa. Pour both shakes into 4 tall glasses at the same time from either side so they sit half and half. Top with whipped cream and a few dark chocolate drops for spots.

note.text: Fifteen puppies and not one of them can say no to a second helping. Roger, more dinner. The little ones are always hungry.

steps.text: Lay out one pastry sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Scatter over the cheddar, parmesan, olives and nigella seeds.
Lay the second sheet on top and press down firmly.

dishes.n: Barn honey shortbread with warm milk dip
dishes.make_ahead: Shortbread up to 3 days in an airtight tin

steps.text: Beat the butter, sugar and some of the honey until pale.
Mix in the flour and salt.
Press into a lined tin and prick all over.
Bake at 160C until pale gold.
Cut into fingers while warm, then cool in the tin.
Warm the milk with the remaining honey and the vanilla. Serve in small cups for dunking.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, assemble and bake when needed

steps.text: Dice the onion and grate the carrots.
Brown the mince with the onion and carrot in the olive oil.
Add the peas and stock and simmer until thick, then season with salt and pepper.
Peel and chop the potatoes, boil until tender, then mash with butter and milk.
Spread the mince in a dish and top with the mash.
Bake at 200C until golden.

veg.make_ahead: Up to 1 day, assemble and bake when needed

steps.text: Dice the onion and grate the carrots.
Brown the mushrooms with the onion and carrot in the oil, then stir in the tomato paste.
Add the lentils, peas and stock and simmer until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and chop the potatoes, boil until tender, then mash with butter and milk.
Spread the lentils in a dish and top with the mash.
Bake at 200C until golden.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 2 days in an airtight tin

steps.text: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg.
Mix in the flour and buttermilk.
Spoon rounds onto lined trays.
Bake at 180C until set and lightly golden.
Cool on the trays.
Mix the icing sugar with the water and vanilla into a glaze, then stir the cocoa into half of it to make a chocolate glaze. Ice half of each cookie with each.
Leave to set.

dishes.make_ahead: Best blended just before serving; whip the cream and chill the glasses up to 2 hours ahead

steps.text: Blend the vanilla ice cream with half the milk and the vanilla. Pour into a jug.
Blend the chocolate ice cream with the remaining milk and the cocoa. Pour into a second jug.
Pour both shakes into tall glasses at the same time from either side so they sit half and half.
Top with whipped cream and chocolate drops for spots.
